Instrument.name: Lunar Laser Ranging Instrument
Instrument.description: LLRI (Lunar Laser Ranging Instrument) is one of the scientific instrument hosted on the Chandrayaan-1 Orbiter. LLRI is a pulsed laser ranging instrument aimed at enhanced study of the moon's surface. Advantages of the laser instrumentation were that they can be readily optimized for any given mission scenario. An added advantage is that they can operate from orbiting spacecraft putting comparatively minimal requirements on spacecraft resources in terms of mass, size and electrical power. Being active instruments, laser measurements can be obtained from both the dark and sunlit portion of the moon, thereby significantly increasing the useful observational coverage. The LLRI instrument for Chandrayaan-1 is produce a sensor footprint of approximately 32 m on the lunar surface and capable of making lunar topography measurements with a resolution of less than 5m.
